auth_provider.description: Authentication provider named in the login request: `db` (the default) for users of the Superset database, `ldap` for an instance with `AUTH_TYPE = AUTH_LDAP`. Can also be set with the `SUPERSET_AUTH_PROVIDER` environment variable.

csrf_enabled.description: Whether to request a CSRF token from Superset and send it with every write request. Defaults to `true`, which is required by a Superset instance with the default `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED = True`. Set it to `false` for an instance where CSRF protection is disabled to skip the extra request before each write operation.

host.description: The URL of the Superset instance. This should include the protocol (http or https) and the hostname or IP address. Example: 'https://superset.example.com'.

password.description: The password to authenticate with Superset. This value is sensitive and will not be displayed in logs or state files.

username.description: The username to authenticate with Superset. This user should have the necessary permissions to manage resources within Superset.

validate_credentials.description: Whether to validate the connection settings and log in to Superset when the provider is configured. Defaults to `true`. When `false`, the provider does not send any request until a resource or data source calls the Superset API, and `host`, `username` and `password` may be left empty. This allows declaring the provider in configurations where Superset is not available and no Superset resources are managed.

block.description: Superset provider for managing Superset resources. The provider logs in to Superset when it is configured; set `validate_credentials = false` to defer it until the first API call.

end_dttm.description: End of the annotation, in the same format, not before the start. Equal to the start for an instant.

json_metadata.description: JSON document with extra settings of the annotation.

layer_id.description: Identifier of the annotation layer. Changing it replaces the annotation.

short_descr.description: Title of the annotation, unique within the layer.

start_dttm.description: Start of the annotation, as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` without a time zone, for example `2026-01-15T00:00:00`.

block.description: Manages an annotation of an annotation layer: an event, or a period, that charts show on their time axis when they display the layer.
Manages an annotation layer: a named group of annotations that charts can display as event markers.

chart_ids.description: Identifiers of the imported charts, keyed by the uuid of their export.

content_hash.description: Hash of the files of the bundle. A change of the files plans an import.

dashboard_ids.description: Identifiers of the imported dashboards, keyed by the uuid of their export.

database_passwords.description: Passwords of the databases of the bundle, needed when a database is created by the import. Keyed by the path of the database file inside the bundle, such as `databases/warehouse.yaml`, or by the file name alone, such as `warehouse.yaml`.

dataset_ids.description: Identifiers of the imported datasets, keyed by the uuid of their export.

files.description: The files of the bundle, keyed by their path in the export layout, such as `dashboards/sales.yaml` or `databases/warehouse.yaml`, with their YAML content as values. The provider zips them with a `metadata.yaml` of the right type, as it does for a directory in `source`. Use it instead of `source` where the provider cannot read files, for example when it runs in a controller. Exactly one of `source` and `files` must be set.

source.description: Directory in the export layout of Superset (`dashboards/`, `charts/`, `datasets/`, `databases/`, `queries/`), or an export zip file. A directory is bundled by the provider with a `metadata.yaml` of the `assets` type. Exactly one of `source` and `files` must be set.

sparse.description: Whether the dashboards of the bundle may reference charts that exist in Superset but are not in the bundle. Recent versions of Superset only. Defaults to `false`.

ssh_tunnel_passwords.description: Passwords of the SSH tunnels of the databases of the bundle. Keyed by the path of the database file inside the bundle, such as `databases/warehouse.yaml`, or by the file name alone, such as `warehouse.yaml`.

ssh_tunnel_private_key_passwords.description: Passphrases of the private keys of the SSH tunnels of the databases of the bundle. Keyed by the path of the database file inside the bundle, such as `databases/warehouse.yaml`, or by the file name alone, such as `warehouse.yaml`.

ssh_tunnel_private_keys.description: Private keys of the SSH tunnels of the databases of the bundle. Keyed by the path of the database file inside the bundle, such as `databases/warehouse.yaml`, or by the file name alone, such as `warehouse.yaml`.

block.description: Imports a whole export bundle at once through the assets endpoint: its databases, datasets, charts, dashboards and saved queries, overwriting the ones that exist, and imports it again whenever its files change. Destroying the resource deletes the imported dashboards, charts and datasets, in that order; the databases stay.

cache_timeout.description: Duration in seconds for which the chart data is cached. Unset to use the timeout of the dataset or database.

certified_by.description: Person or group that certified the chart.

datasource_id.description: Identifier of the dataset the chart is built on.

datasource_type.description: Type of the datasource: `table` (a dataset, the default), `query`, `saved_query` or `view`.

owners.description: Identifiers of the users who own the chart. Defaults to the user the provider authenticates as.

params.description: JSON document with the form data of the chart, as shown in the chart's `View query` and `Edit chart properties` dialogs. Formatting differences are not reported as drift.

query_context.description: JSON document with the query context of the chart, which Superset uses for alerts, reports and cache warm-up. When unset, the query context Superset generates on its own is left alone.

tags.description: Names of the tags attached to the chart, with the `TAGGING_SYSTEM` feature flag. When unset, the tags are left as they are; when set, the chart has exactly these tags. Tags that do not exist yet are created, and stay when the chart is destroyed.

block.description: Manages a chart. Place a chart on a dashboard through the `position_json` of the dashboard.

ssh_tunnel_private_keys.description: Private keys of the SSH tunnels of the databases of the bundle. Keyed by the path of the database file inside the bundle, such as `databases/warehouse.yaml`, or by the file name alone, such as `warehouse.yaml`.

template_name.description: Name of the template as shown in Superset.

block.description: Manages a CSS template: a reusable stylesheet that can be applied to dashboards.

certified_by.description: Person or group that certified the dashboard.

json_metadata.description: JSON document with the settings of the dashboard, such as `refresh_frequency`, `color_scheme` or `native_filter_configuration`. Only the keys set here are managed: keys Superset adds or that are changed in the UI keep their value and are not reported as drift. When unset, the settings are left to Superset.

owners.description: Identifiers of the users who own the dashboard. Defaults to the user the provider authenticates as.

position_json.description: JSON document with the layout of the dashboard. The charts referenced by its `CHART` elements are linked to the dashboard. Superset adds the `uuid` of each chart to the layout, which is not reported as drift. When unset, the layout is left to Superset.

published.description: Whether the dashboard is published; an unpublished dashboard is a draft visible to its owners only. Defaults to `false`.

roles.description: Identifiers of the roles granted access to the dashboard when dashboard role-based access control is enabled.

slug.description: Unique slug used in the URL of the dashboard instead of its id.

tags.description: Names of the tags attached to the dashboard, with the `TAGGING_SYSTEM` feature flag. When unset, the tags are left as they are; when set, the dashboard has exactly these tags. Tags that do not exist yet are created, and stay when the dashboard is destroyed.

theme_id.description: Identifier of the `superset_theme` the dashboard applies, on Superset 6. Unset, the dashboard uses the theme of the instance.

block.description: Manages a dashboard. The charts shown on the dashboard are the charts placed in its `position_json`.

allowed_domains.description: Origins allowed to embed the dashboard, for example `https://app.example.com`. An empty set allows every origin.

dashboard_id.description: Identifier of the dashboard to embed. Changing it replaces the configuration, which gives the embedded dashboard a new uuid.

id.description: Identifier of the embedding configuration, which is the identifier of the dashboard.

uuid.description: Identifier under which the embedded SDK loads the dashboard.

block.description: Makes a dashboard embeddable in other applications with the Superset embedded SDK. Guest tokens for the embedded dashboard require the `EMBEDDED_SUPERSET` feature flag in Superset.

ssh_tunnel_private_keys.description: Private keys of the SSH tunnels of the databases of the bundle. Keyed by the path of the database file inside the bundle, such as `databases/warehouse.yaml`, or by the file name alone, such as `warehouse.yaml`.

allow_ctas.description: Whether `CREATE TABLE AS` is allowed in SQL Lab.

allow_cvas.description: Whether `CREATE VIEW AS` is allowed in SQL Lab.

allow_dml.description: Whether DML statements are allowed in SQL Lab.

allow_file_upload.description: Whether files can be uploaded into the database. The allowed schemas are set in `extra` as `schemas_allowed_for_file_upload`. Defaults to `false`.

allow_run_async.description: Whether SQL Lab queries run asynchronously through Celery.

cache_timeout.description: Duration in seconds for which the charts of the database are cached. When unset, the value is left as it is in Superset: the timeout of the Superset instance for a new connection.

db_engine.description: SQLAlchemy dialect of the connection, for example `postgresql` or `mysql+pymysql`. Required with the other parts when `sqlalchemy_uri` is not set.

db_pass.description: Password of the connection. It is inserted into the URI as is, so percent-encode special characters or use `sqlalchemy_uri`.

expose_in_sqllab.description: Whether the connection is available in SQL Lab.

extra.description: JSON document with the extra configuration of the connection, such as `engine_params`, `metadata_params` or `schemas_allowed_for_file_upload`. Defaults to `{"client_encoding": "utf8"}` when the connection is created without it.

force_ctas_schema.description: Schema in which `CREATE TABLE AS` creates its tables when the query does not name one.

id.description: Numeric identifier of the database connection.

impersonate_user.description: Whether queries run as the logged-in user instead of the user of the connection. Defaults to `false`.

masked_encrypted_extra.description: JSON document with the encrypted extra configuration of the connection, such as the credentials of BigQuery or Google Sheets. Superset masks it in its responses, so changes made in the UI are not detected.

server_cert.description: CA bundle, in PEM format, used to validate the certificate of the database server.

sqlalchemy_uri.description: Full SQLAlchemy URI of the connection, for engines whose URI does not fit the parts, for example `awsathena+rest://...` or `trino://...`. Conflicts with the parts. Changes made to the URI in the Superset UI are not detected, because Superset masks the password in the URI it returns.

password.description: Password of the user. Conflicts with `private_key`.

private_key.description: RSA private key of the user, in PEM format. Conflicts with `password`.

ssh_tunnel.description: SSH tunnel through which Superset reaches the database. Requires the `SSH_TUNNELING` feature flag in Superset. Superset authenticates with either `password` or `private_key`; the private key must be an RSA key.

block.description: Manages a database connection. The connection is given either as a full `sqlalchemy_uri` or as its parts (`db_engine`, `db_user`, `db_pass`, `db_host`, `db_port` and `db_name`). Superset tests the connection when it is created or updated.

database_id.description: Numeric identifier of the database connection to sync.

id.description: Numeric identifier of the database connection.

triggers.description: Arbitrary values whose change runs the sync again, for example the list of schemas of the source.

block.description: Makes Superset 6 refresh the permissions of the catalogs and schemas of a database connection, as the *Sync permissions* action of the connection does, so roles can be granted `catalog_access` and `schema_access` on what the source gained. The sync runs when the resource is created and again whenever `database_id` or `triggers` change; it is not undone when the resource is destroyed.

always_filter_main_dttm.description: Whether the time range of a chart is always applied to the main datetime column, even when the chart filters another one. Defaults to `false`.

cache_timeout.description: Duration in seconds for which the charts of the dataset are cached. Unset to use the timeout of the database.

column_name.description: Name of the column, unique within the dataset.

expression.description: SQL expression of a calculated column, for example `amount * 100`.

filterable.description: Whether the column can be used in a filter. Defaults to `true` in Superset.

groupby.description: Whether the column can be used as a dimension. Defaults to `true` in Superset.

is_dttm.description: Whether the column is a datetime column, which can be used as the time column of a chart. Superset detects it for the columns of the source.

python_date_format.description: Format of the values of a datetime column stored as text, for example `%Y-%m-%d`, or `epoch_s`.

type.description: Data type of the column, for example `NUMERIC`. Superset detects it for the columns of the source; set it for a calculated column.

verbose_name.description: Label shown instead of the name.

columns.description: Columns of the dataset. When unset, the columns are left to Superset, which detects them from the source. When set, the dataset has exactly these columns, and columns not listed here are deleted. Within a column, only the attributes that are set are written, so the others keep the value Superset has, such as the detected `type`; an empty string clears an attribute.

database_name.description: Name of the database connection the dataset belongs to. Changing it replaces the dataset.

default_endpoint.description: URL Superset redirects to when the dataset is opened.

extra.description: JSON document with extra settings of the dataset, such as `certification` or `warning_markdown`.

fetch_values_predicate.description: SQL predicate applied when Superset fetches the distinct values of a column for a filter.

filter_select_enabled.description: Whether filters of the dataset offer the distinct values of a column. Defaults to `true`.

main_dttm_col.description: Column used as the default time column of the dataset. Superset picks the first datetime column when unset.

d3format.description: D3 format of the values, for example `,.2f`.

expression.description: SQL aggregate expression of the metric, for example `SUM(amount)`.

metric_name.description: Name of the metric, unique within the dataset.

metric_type.description: Type of the aggregate, for example `sum` or `count`; informational.

verbose_name.description: Label shown instead of the name.

warning_text.description: Warning shown next to the metric.

metrics.description: Metrics of the dataset. When unset, the metrics are left to Superset, which creates `count` with every dataset. When set, the dataset has exactly these metrics: declare `count` too if it should stay, and metrics not listed here are deleted.

normalize_columns.description: Whether the names of the columns are normalized to lower case when they are fetched from the source. Defaults to `false`.

owners.description: Identifiers of the users who own the dataset. Defaults to the user the provider authenticates as.

perm.description: View menu of the `datasource_access` permission of the dataset, `[<database>].[<table>](id:<id>)`, for `superset_role_permissions`.

schema_perm.description: View menu of the `schema_access` permission of the schema of the dataset, `[<database>].[<schema>]`; null without a schema.

sql.description: SQL query of a virtual dataset. Superset runs it when the dataset is created to detect the columns, so it must be valid at that time: Jinja templates need the `ENABLE_TEMPLATE_PROCESSING` feature flag, and on Superset 3.1, whose create endpoint does not take `template_params`, their parameters need a default such as `{{ region | default('eu') }}`.

table_name.description: Name of the table, or name of the virtual dataset.

template_params.description: JSON object with the default values of the Jinja template parameters of the SQL query. Recent versions of Superset apply them when the dataset is created; Superset 3.1 only after.

block.description: Manages a dataset: a table of a database, or a virtual dataset defined by a SQL query. Superset detects the columns of the dataset and creates its `count` metric itself; `columns` and `metrics` take them over when set.

sync_columns.description: Whether the columns of datasets that already exist are replaced by the columns of the bundle. Defaults to `false`.

sync_metrics.description: Whether the metrics of datasets that already exist are replaced by the metrics of the bundle. Defaults to `false`.

dataset_id.description: Numeric identifier of the dataset to sync.

triggers.description: Arbitrary values whose change runs the sync again, for example the version of the source table.

block.description: Syncs the columns of a dataset from its source, as the *Sync columns from source* button of the dataset editor does: Superset adds the columns the source gained, removes the ones it lost, updates the type of the ones it has, and recreates the `count` metric when it is missing. The sync runs when the resource is created and again whenever `dataset_id` or `triggers` change; it is not undone when the resource is destroyed.

label.description: Label shown instead of the name.

name.description: Name of the group, unique in Superset.

roles.description: Identifiers of the roles the members of the group get, for example from `superset_role`.

users.description: Identifiers of the members of the group, for example from `superset_user`.

block.description: Manages a group of users, on Superset 6: its members get the roles of the group. The group endpoints belong to the Flask-AppBuilder security API, which Superset only enables with `FAB_ADD_SECURITY_API = True`.

allowed_databases.description: List of database names that can be accessed through this meta connection.

database_name.description: Name of the meta database connection.

expose_in_sqllab.description: Whether to expose this connection in SQL Lab.

id.description: Numeric identifier of the meta database connection.

is_managed_externally.description: Whether this connection is managed externally.

sqlalchemy_uri.description: SQLAlchemy URI for the meta database connection. Defaults to 'superset://' for meta databases.

block.description: Manages a meta database connection in Superset for cross-database queries.

active.description: Whether the schedule runs. Defaults to `true`.

chart_id.description: Identifier of the chart to send. Set either `chart_id` or `dashboard_id`.

context_markdown.description: Markdown text sent with the content.

crontab.description: Schedule as a cron expression, for example `0 9 * * 1` for every Monday at 09:00.

custom_width.description: Width in pixels of the screenshot of the content.

dashboard_id.description: Identifier of the dashboard to send. Set either `chart_id` or `dashboard_id`.

database_name.description: Name of the database connection an alert runs its query on. Alerts only.

email_subject.description: Subject of the email, on recent versions of Superset.

extra.description: JSON document with extra settings, such as the tabs of a dashboard to send: `{"dashboard": {"activeTabs": ["TAB-id"]}}`.

force_screenshot.description: Whether the screenshot is always taken fresh instead of served from the cache. Defaults to `false`.

grace_period.description: Seconds during which an alert that was already sent is not sent again. Defaults to the value Superset picks, usually 14400.

log_retention.description: Days the execution logs are kept. Defaults to the value Superset picks, usually 90.

name.description: Name of the report, unique among the reports or among the alerts.

owners.description: Identifiers of the users who own the report. Defaults to the user the provider authenticates as.

bcc.description: Addresses in blind copy of an email, on recent versions of Superset.

cc.description: Addresses in copy of an email, on recent versions of Superset.

target.description: Addresses separated by commas, a Slack channel, or a webhook URL.

type.description: `Email` or `Slack`; recent versions of Superset also take `SlackV2` and `Webhook`.

recipients.description: Destinations of the report, at least one. Superset 3.1 ignores an empty list, so the recipients can only be replaced, not all removed.

report_format.description: Format of the content: `PNG`, `CSV`, `TEXT`, or `PDF` on recent versions of Superset. Defaults to `PNG`.

sql.description: SQL query of an alert, which must return a single value. Alerts only.

timezone.description: Time zone of the schedule, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Defaults to the one Superset picks, usually `UTC`.

type.description: `Report` sends the content on every run; `Alert` runs the SQL query and sends the content when the condition is met.

validator_threshold.description: Value the result of the query is compared with by the `operator` condition.

validator_type.description: Condition of an alert: `not null` triggers when the query returns a value, `operator` compares it with `validator_threshold`. Alerts only.

working_timeout.description: Seconds a run may take before it is marked as failed. Defaults to the value Superset picks, usually 3600.

block.description: Manages a report or an alert of the Alerts & Reports page: a chart or a dashboard sent to recipients on a schedule, or, for an alert, when a SQL query meets a condition. The `ALERT_REPORTS` feature flag must be on, and Superset needs its workers to actually send anything.
Manages a role in Superset. Requires the Flask-AppBuilder security API, which Superset enables with `FAB_ADD_SECURITY_API = True` in `superset_config.py`.

id.description: The unique identifier for the role permissions resource.

last_updated.description: The timestamp of the last update to the role permissions.

id.description: The unique identifier of the permission.

view_menu.description: The name of the view menu associated with the permission.

resource_permissions.description: A list of permissions associated with the role.

role_name.description: The name of the role to which the permissions are assigned.

block.description: Manages the permissions associated with a role in Superset. Requires the Flask-AppBuilder security API, which Superset enables with `FAB_ADD_SECURITY_API = True` in `superset_config.py`.

clause.description: SQL expression added to the WHERE clause, for example `region = 'EMEA'`.

filter_type.description: `Regular` applies the clause to the queries of the listed roles; `Base` applies it to everyone except the listed roles. Defaults to `Regular`.

group_key.description: Rules that share a group key are combined with OR, rules with different keys with AND.

roles.description: Identifiers of the roles the rule applies to (or is excluded from, for a `Base` rule). Defaults to none.

tables.description: Identifiers of the datasets the rule applies to.

block.description: Manages a row level security rule: a SQL clause that Superset adds to the queries of the given datasets for the members of the given roles.

catalog.description: Default catalog the query runs in. Only Superset 4.1 and later support catalogs.

database_id.description: Identifier of the database connection the query runs against.

id.description: Numeric identifier of the saved query.

label.description: Name of the saved query as shown in SQL Lab.

schema.description: Default schema the query runs in.

template_parameters.description: JSON object with the Jinja template parameters of the query.

block.description: Manages a query saved in SQL Lab.

name.description: Name of the tag, unique in Superset.

block.description: Manages a tag, a label attached to charts, dashboards and saved queries with the `TAGGING_SYSTEM` feature flag. The objects a tag is attached to are managed by the `tags` of `superset_chart` and `superset_dashboard`; the tag keeps them when it is renamed, and is detached from them when it is destroyed.

json_data.description: JSON document with the design tokens of the theme, as the theme editor exports it, for example `{"token": {"colorPrimary": "#1f77b4"}}`.

system_dark.description: Whether the theme is the dark theme of the instance. Only one theme is. Defaults to `false`.

system_default.description: Whether the theme is the default theme of the instance. Only one theme is, so setting it on a theme takes the place of the previous one. Defaults to `false`.

uuid.description: UUID of the theme, as export bundles reference it.

block.description: Manages a theme of the Superset UI, on Superset 6: a JSON document of design tokens that a `superset_dashboard` applies with `theme_id`, and that can be the default or the dark theme of the whole instance.

active.description: Whether the user is active. Defaults to true.

password.description: Password of the user. Required for creation, optional for updates.

roles.description: List of role IDs assigned to the user.

block.description: Manages a user in Superset. Requires the Flask-AppBuilder security API, which Superset enables with `FAB_ADD_SECURITY_API = True` in `superset_config.py`.

datasource_id.description: Identifier of the dataset of the chart. Set it when several charts share the name.

datasource_type.description: Type of the dataset of the chart, usually `table`.

name.description: Name of the chart. The comparison is exact.

url.description: Path of the chart in Superset.

viz_type.description: Visualization type of the chart, for example `echarts_timeseries_line`.

block.description: Looks up a chart by its name, for example to place it on a dashboard or to send it with `superset_report`. Chart names are not unique in Superset: the lookup fails when no chart matches, or when several do.

template_name.description: Name of the template. The comparison is exact.

block.description: Looks up a CSS template by its name. The lookup fails when no template has exactly that name.

slug.description: Slug of the dashboard, the last part of its URL. Set either `slug` or `title`.

title.description: Title of the dashboard. The comparison is exact. Set either `slug` or `title`.

url.description: Path of the dashboard in Superset.

block.description: Looks up a dashboard by its slug or its title, for example to embed it with `superset_dashboard_embedding` or to send it with `superset_report`. Slugs are unique; titles are not, so a lookup by title fails when several dashboards share it.

allow_dml.description: Whether SQL Lab may run statements that modify data.

backend.description: SQLAlchemy dialect of the connection, for example `postgresql`.

database_name.description: Name of the connection. The comparison is exact.

expose_in_sqllab.description: Whether the connection is available in SQL Lab.

uuid.description: UUID of the connection, as export bundles reference it.

block.description: Looks up a database connection by its name, for example to reference its id or to check its settings. The lookup fails when no connection has exactly that name.
Lists the schemas Superset sees in a database connection, for example to create a dataset for every table of a schema that exists.

comment.description: Comment of the column in the database.

long_type.description: Full type of the column, for example `NUMERIC(10, 2)`.

type.description: Generic type of the column, for example `NUMERIC`.

columns.description: Columns of the table, in the order of the database.

comment.description: Comment of the table in the database.

table_name.description: Name of the table or view.

block.description: Describes a table or a view as Superset reads it from the database: its columns and their types, for example to declare the `columns` of a `superset_dataset`.

name.description: Name of the table or view.

tables.description: Tables and views of the schema, sorted by name.

block.description: Lists the tables and views Superset sees in a schema of a database connection, for example to create a dataset for each of them.
Fetches the list of databases from Superset.

database_id.description: Numeric identifier of the database connection.

database_name.description: Name of the database connection. Set it when several datasets share the table name.

kind.description: `physical` for a table, `virtual` for a query.

perm.description: View menu of the `datasource_access` permission of the dataset, for `superset_role_permissions`.

schema.description: Schema of the table. Set it when several datasets share the table name.

schema_perm.description: View menu of the `schema_access` permission of the schema of the dataset; null without a schema.

sql.description: SQL query of a virtual dataset; null for a table.

table_name.description: Name of the table, or name of the virtual dataset. The comparison is exact.

block.description: Looks up a dataset by its table name, narrowed down by its schema and database connection, for example to reference its id in a chart or its permission in `superset_role_permissions`. The lookup fails when no dataset matches, or when several do.

database_id.description: Database ID to which the dataset belongs.

database_name.description: Database name to which the dataset belongs.

owners.description: List of owners of the dataset.

block.description: Fetches all datasets from Superset.

name.description: Name of the role. The comparison is exact.

block.description: Looks up a role by its name, for example to reference its id in `superset_user.roles` without hard-coding it. The lookup fails when no role has exactly that name.

view_menu_name.description: Name of the view menu associated with the permission.

block.description: Fetches the permissions for a role from Superset.
Fetches the list of roles from Superset.

roles.description: List of roles assigned to the user.

block.description: Fetches the list of users from Superset.
